evidence_boundaries: Standard-source spectra, peak areas, source distances and the 367.7 keV sum peak are direct measurements; the 1.2 mm dead layer, angular biasing, PHITS efficiency response, Gaussian broadening and Efftran CSF are model-assisted.
The 1.2 mm dead layer is primarily constrained by the 121 and 344 keV response; it is not a sub-percent validation across all energies and geometries.
At 3.8 cm the TCS correction reduces energy-dependent bias, but the remaining 6.51 to 8.46 percent residual stays outside the stated 5 percent acceptance band.
Table 2 supports an uncorrected maximum deviation of about 14.7 percent, not the conclusion's statement that it exceeded 20 percent.
This is not a laser-plasma or converter-target experiment and does not validate pulsed pile-up, EMP, prompt-gamma background, broad-spectrum activation, shielding or shot-to-shot source stability.
No PHITS or Efftran run, peak-area reanalysis, dead-layer fit or experimental replay was performed locally.
